card.band: 20h tier. The incremental LLVM build is slow, and the worklist invariants are subtle: a missed re-queue changes the output and trips the gate. A frontier agent finishes the loop removal in some trials but misses the full speedup on average. A weaker model breaks equivalence or never gets a build that works.
card.cheat: Skipping transforms or capping iterations changes IR and fails the equivalence gate. Hidden IR is out of the image. Prebuilt reference binaries are absent and the upstream tree is snapshotted without history.
card.grading: Hard gate: opt output on a few thousand hidden .ll inputs (generated by mutating and reducing public IR and the LLVM test inputs, not shipped) must be semantically equal to the reference opt. Equality is a normalised textual diff, plus an alive-style check on small functions. Score is the median wall-clock of opt -passes=instcombine,... over large hidden IR modules, against the untouched build.
card.reference: The upstream LLVM 18 InstCombine change set, adapted to the trimmed tree. The article gives ~4% end-to-end gain, and a larger one when InstCombine runs alone. The speedup S is measured on our own hidden modules, not copied from the article.
card.source: https://developers.redhat.com/articles/2023/12/07/how-single-iteration-instcombine-improves-llvm-compile-time ; LLVM commit before the fixpoint-loop removal -> LLVM 18; Apache-2.0 with LLVM Exceptions
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot of the pre-LLVM-18 tree trimmed to the opt tool, X86 backend and the InstCombine/InstSimplify/analysis libraries, with a ninja build. The agent restructures InstCombine to a single worklist iteration (program-order deferred worklist, shared IRBuilder, in-visit unreachable handling) without changing optimised IR. Delivery is the rebuilt opt binary.
card.title: LLVM InstCombine single-pass compile-time speedup

source_notes: Levers: drop fixpoint loop, fix worklist handling in transforms, shared IRBuilder via virtual methods, deferred worklist in program order, reverse post-order traversal, unreachable-code handling in-visit, tests run 2 iterations to verify fixpoint. Page compares commits not releases. single-source; the LLVM compile-time tracker (llvm-compile-time-tracker.com) is the data source but its own licence is not stated on the page and per-commit changes are mostly under 0.1%

facts.claim: Red Hat article by Nikita Popov (2023-12-07) describes the single-iteration InstCombine change and says it will be part of LLVM 18
About 4% end-to-end compile-time reduction on CTMark (instructions:u, compare range 19a1b67 to 4189584)
A separate, larger InstCombine-only compile-time gain is reported
The fixpoint iteration was introduced in commit 960a54303730a86694934cb89efe9bc501e25b91
Upstream commit titled '[InstCombine] Only perform one iteration' removes the outer fixpoint loop (landed commit hash not confirmed at source; seen only in a search snippet from a third-party mirror)
LLVM is licensed under Apache License v2.0 with LLVM Exceptions

Task says the optimised IR is kept unchanged by the single-iteration restructure; the article says an extra iteration was needed in 0.04% of cases, so the upstream change does alter output on rare inputs
Article reports 22.3% of llvm-test-suite cases ran a verification-only extra iteration and 0.04% needed an extra iteration

v1.kill_reason: Acceptance breadth fails: the gate requires textual equality with the reference opt, but the task leaves worklist order to the agent (program-order deferred worklist, RPO), and textual IR output depends on fold order, so a valid alternative restructuring would fail. The reference itself also changes output on rare inputs (article: 0.04% extra-iteration cases), contradicting "without changing optimised IR". Repair: gate on alive/semantic equivalence plus a canonicalised form, and measure the speedup with repeated runs. Re-validate after that change; the spike plan tests whether the noise and output-difference rates allow it.

Band.why: No dated public evidence of frontier-agent results on this kind of work; the article's own numbers (~4% end-to-end, no InstCombine-only figure) leave the reachable S unknown.

Build.why: Estimated 2-4 days to build, set up the reference and stabilise timings; under the 5-day K12 limit.

Fit.why: CPU-only and within 8 cores / 16 GB; opt+X86 build is heavy but feasible, though timing noise on gVisor is a risk.

Hor.why: Long tail of per-transform worklist fixes across many files suits the 20h tier.

Lic.why: Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception confirmed at the LLVM repo; shipping the trimmed tree and reference is allowed.

Multi.why: Levers are interdependent (worklist order, IRBuilder, unreachable handling) and feed one scalar speedup; not steady independent buckets.

Nov.why: Highest l0 neighbour is 0.18 (above 0.15 threshold); not on CROWDED list.

Real.why: Public LLVM source with a Red Hat article and upstream commit history (commit hash 960a5430 confirmed via article).

Ref.why: Permissive upstream change set exists; it is multi-commit and must be adapted to the trimmed tree, so it is not a single clean reference diff.

Seal.why: History-less snapshot keeps the commits out of reach, but the article and upstream design are publicly recallable, so Band must absorb that risk.

Surf.why: Thousands of hidden .ll inputs plus alive-style checks, but the gate is textual equality, which limits useful breadth.

spike_plan.kill_if: Run-to-run noise exceeds the InstCombine-only gain, or textual output differs on a non-trivial share of inputs with no normalisation that makes both builds equal.
spike_plan.pass_if: Single-iteration build gives a measurable InstCombine-only speedup (above run-to-run spread) AND output differences from the fixpoint build are rare enough that an alive-based or canonicalised gate can accept both.
steps: In a throwaway networked container, clone llvm-project and check out the parent of the single-iteration InstCombine commit (verify the hash on the primary repo; the article gives 960a5430 as the fixpoint's origin) and llvmorg-18.1.0.
Build opt with X86 only in both trees with ninja (Release, 8 cores), recording build time and binary size.
Generate ~500 .ll inputs from public llvm/test/Transforms/InstCombine files and a few large modules; run opt -passes=instcombine on each with both builds and diff the textual output.
Count how many inputs differ between the fixpoint and single-iteration builds. If the rate is non-zero, the textual-equality gate fails on upstream itself.
Time opt -passes=instcombine on 5 large modules, 10 runs each, both builds; compute median and run-to-run spread. If the spread exceeds the claimed gain, the reward signal is noise.
Check determinism: run the same binary 3 times on the same input and confirm byte-identical output.

v1.summary: LLVM 18 single-iteration InstCombine is a real, Apache-2.0-with-LLVM-exception subject with a public article and upstream history, which fits the optimization class and the 20h tier. It is killed as specified (K4) because a textual-equality gate cannot accept valid alternative worklist orders and the reference itself changes rare outputs, so the gate needs redesign before re-validation.
